sanskrit: sa bhīmaṃ sahasābhyetya pṛdākuḥ kṣudhito bhṛśam jagrāhājagaro grāho bhujayor ubhayor balāt
english: That serpent, exceedingly hungry, suddenly rushed at Bhīma and seized him like a great python seizing prey, grasping both his arms with force.

sanskrit: tena saṃspṛṣṭamātrasya bhimasenasya vai tadā saṃjñā mumoha sahasā varadānena tasya ha
english: The moment Bhīmasena was touched by it, his consciousness suddenly became confused on account of the boon that had been granted to that serpent.

sanskrit: daśa nāgasahasrāṇi dhārayanti hi yad balam tad balaṃ bhīmasenasya bhujayor asamaṃ paraiḥ
english: The strength that ten thousand elephants possess — that very strength dwelt in the arms of Bhīmasena, unequalled by any foe.

sanskrit: sa tejasvī tathā tena bhujagena vaśīkṛtaḥ visphurañ śanakair bhīmo na śaśāka viceṣṭitum
english: That illustrious one, subdued thus by the serpent, shuddered slightly but could not stir — Bhīma was unable to move at all.

sanskrit: nāgāyutasamaprāṇaḥ siṃhaskandho mahābhujaḥ gṛhīto vyajahāt sattvaṃ varadānena mohitaḥ
english: He whose vitality equalled ten thousand elephants, with lion-like shoulders and mighty arms, was seized and lost his power, bewildered by the boon.

sanskrit: sa hi prayatnam akarot tīvram ātmavimokṣaṇe na cainam aśakad vīraḥ kathaṃ cit pratibādhitum
english: He made a fierce effort to free himself, but that hero was not able by any means to resist or repel the serpent.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa bhīmasenas tejasvī tathā sarpavaśaṃ gataḥ cintayām āsa sarpasya vīryam atyadbhutaṃ mahat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: That illustrious Bhīmasena, having thus fallen under the power of the serpent, began to reflect upon the serpent's strength, which was exceedingly wonderful and great.

sanskrit: uvāca ca mahāsarpaṃ kāmayā brūhi pannaga kas tvaṃ bho bhujagaśreṣṭha kiṃ mayā ca kariṣyasi
english: And he spoke to that great serpent out of curiosity: "Tell me, O snake — who are you, O best among serpents, and what will you do with me?"

sanskrit: pāṇḍavo bhimaseno 'haṃ dharmarājād anantaraḥ nāgāyutasamaprāṇas tvayā nītaḥ kathaṃ vaśam
english: "I am Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, second only to the Dharma-king; I whose vitality equals ten thousand elephants — how have you brought me under your power?"

sanskrit: siṃhāḥ kesariṇo vyāghrā mahiṣā vāraṇās tathā samāgatāś ca bahuśo nihatāś ca mayā mṛdhe
english: "Lions, tigers, buffaloes, and elephants too — many have come against me and have been slain by me in battle."

sanskrit: dānavāś ca piśācāś ca rākṣasāś ca mahābalāḥ bhujavegam aśaktā me soḍhuṃ pannagasattama
english: "Dānavas, Piśācas, and Rākṣasas of great strength have been unable to withstand the speed of my arms, O best of serpents."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vidyābalaṃ kiṃ vā varadānam atho tava udyogam api kurvāṇo vaśago 'smi kṛtas tvayā
english: "Is it the power of learning, or is it a boon granted to you? Even while I was exerting myself, you have placed me entirely under your control."

sanskrit: asatyo vikramo nṝṇām iti me niścitā matiḥ yathedaṃ me tvayā nāga balaṃ pratihataṃ mahat
english: "My mind is now firmly convinced that the valour of men is vain — for you, O serpent, have thus checked my great strength."

sanskrit: ity evaṃvādinaṃ vīraṃ bhīmam akliṣṭakāriṇam bhogena mahatā sarpaḥ samantāt paryaveṣṭayat
english: While the hero Bhīma, the doer of tireless deeds, was speaking thus, the serpent encircled him on all sides with its massive coils.

sanskrit: nigṛhya taṃ mahābāhuṃ tataḥ sa bhujagas tadā vimucyāsya bhujau pīnāv idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having bound that mighty-armed one, and then releasing his stout arms, that serpent spoke these words:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvaṃ kṣudhitasyādya devair bhakṣo mahābhuja diṣṭyā kālasya mahataḥ priyāḥ prāṇā hi dehinām
english: "By good fortune you have been sent today by the gods as food for me who am hungry, O mighty-armed one — for indeed, dear to all embodied beings is life in the face of great time."

sanskrit: yathā tv idaṃ mayā prāptaṃ bhujaṃgatvam ariṃdama tad avaśyaṃ mayā khyāpyaṃ tavādya śṛṇu sattama
english: "But as to how I have come to be a serpent, O tamer of foes — that I must relate to you today; listen, O best of beings."

sanskrit: imām avasthāṃ saṃprāpto hy ahaṃ kopān manīṣiṇām śāpasyāntaṃ pariprepsuḥ sarpasya kathayāmi tat
english: "I arrived at this condition through the wrath of the wise; now seeking the end of the serpent's curse, I shall tell you of it."

sanskrit: nahuṣo nāma rājarṣir vyaktaṃ te śrotram āgataḥ tavaiva pūrvaḥ pūrveṣām āyor vaṃśakaraḥ sutaḥ
english: "The royal sage named Nahuṣa — of whom you have surely heard — I am he, the ancestor of your ancestors, the son of Āyu, founder of your lineage."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ śāpād agastyasya brāhmaṇān avamanya ca imām avasthām āpannaḥ paśya daivam idaṃ mama
english: "I, having disrespected the Brāhmaṇas and through the curse of Agastya, have fallen into this condition. Behold what fate has done to me."

sanskrit: tvāṃ ced avadhyam āyāntam atīva priyadarśanam aham adyopayokṣyāmi vidhānaṃ paśya yādṛśam
english: "Though you are one who should not be slain, coming here so very fair to behold, I shall devour you today — see what my situation is like."

sanskrit: na hi me mucyate kaś cit kathaṃ cid grahaṇaṃ gataḥ gajo vā mahiṣo vāpi ṣaṭhe kāle narottama
english: "No one, once seized by me, is released by any means — whether elephant or buffalo — at the sixth meal-time, O best of men."

sanskrit: nāsi kevalasarpeṇa tiryagyoniṣu vartatā gṛhītaḥ kauravaśreṣṭha varadānam idaṃ mama
english: "You are not seized merely by a common serpent dwelling among animals — this is the boon that is mine, O best of the Kauravas."

sanskrit: patatā hi vimānāgrān mayā śakrāsanād drutam kuru śāpāntam ity ukto bhagavān munisattamaḥ
english: "For when I was falling headlong from the summit of my celestial car, fleeing swiftly from Indra's throne, the blessed sage, the best of munis, said to me: 'Bring the curse to its end.'"

sanskrit: sa mām uvāca tejasvī kṛpayābhipariplutaḥ mokṣas te bhavitā rājan kasmāc cit kālaparyayāt
english: "That illustrious one, filled with compassion, spoke to me: 'Your release shall come, O king, through the turn of time in some way.'"

sanskrit: tato 'smi patito bhūmau na ca mām ajahāt smṛtiḥ smārtam asti purāṇaṃ me yathaivādhigataṃ tathā
english: "Then I fell to the earth, and my memory did not leave me; the ancient knowledge that I had acquired remains with me as it was."

sanskrit: yas tu te vyāhṛtān praśnān pratibrūyād viśeṣavit sa tvāṃ mokṣayitā śāpād iti mām abravīd ṛṣiḥ
english: "'He who shall knowledgeably answer the questions put to you shall be your liberator from the curse' — thus the sage told me."

sanskrit: gṛhītasya tvayā rājan prāṇino 'pi balīyasaḥ sattvabhraṃśo 'dhikasyāpi sarvasyāśu bhaviṣyati
english: "'Of every living creature seized by you, O king, however strong, however great, the loss of vital power will come swiftly to all.'"

sanskrit: iti cāpy aham aśrauṣaṃ vacas teṣāṃ dayāvatām mayi saṃjātahārdānām atha te 'ntarhitā dvijāḥ
english: "Thus did I hear the words of those compassionate ones who had become tender-hearted toward me — and then those Brāhmaṇas disappeared."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ paramaduṣkarmā vasāmi niraye 'śucau sarpayonim imāṃ prāpya kālākāṅkṣī mahādyute
english: "I, of most wicked deeds, dwell in this impure hell, having attained this serpent-birth, awaiting the right time, O greatly resplendent one."

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahābāhur bhīmaseno bhujaṃgamam na te kupye mahāsarpa na cātmānaṃ vigarhaye
english: The mighty-armed Bhīmasena then said to that serpent: "I am not angry with you, O great serpent, nor do I blame myself."

sanskrit: yasmād abhāvī bhāvī vā manuṣyaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ āgame yadi vāpāye na tatra glapayen manaḥ
english: "Because whether a man will or will not experience pleasure and pain — when they come or when they depart, the mind should not be distressed about that."

sanskrit: daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa ko nivartitum arhati daivam eva paraṃ manye puruṣārtho nirarthakaḥ
english: "Who is able to turn back fate by human effort? I consider fate alone supreme; human effort is without purpose."

sanskrit: paśya daivopaghātād dhi bhujavīryavyapāśrayam imām avasthāṃ saṃprāptam animittam ihādya mām
english: "Behold me here today, brought to this condition without cause, though I had recourse to the strength of my arms — through the blow of fate."

sanskrit: kiṃ tu nādyānuśocāmi tathātmānaṃ vināśitam yathā tu vipine nyastān bhrātṝn rājyaparicyutān
english: "Yet I do not grieve today for myself being thus destroyed as much as for my brothers cast into the forest, dispossessed of their kingdom."

sanskrit: himavāṃś ca sudurgo 'yaṃ yakṣarākṣasasaṃkulaḥ māṃ ca te samudīkṣantaḥ prapatiṣyanti vihvalāḥ
english: "This Himavat is very difficult to traverse, filled with Yakṣas and Rākṣasas — and they, looking out for me, will fall into distress."

sanskrit: vinaṣṭam atha vā śrutvā bhaviṣyanti nirudyamāḥ dharmaśīlā mayā te hi bādhyante rājyagṛddhinā
english: "Or upon hearing of my death they will become disheartened and listless — those virtuous ones who have been oppressed by me who am greedy for the kingdom."

sanskrit: atha vā nārjuno dhīmān viṣādam upayāsyati sarvāstravid anādhṛṣyo devagandharvarākṣasaiḥ
english: "Surely wise Arjuna will not fall into despondency — he who knows all weapons and is invincible to gods, Gandharvas, and Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: samarthaḥ sa mahābāhur ekāhnā sumahābalaḥ devarājam api sthānāt pracyāvayitum ojasā
english: "That mighty-armed one of immense strength is capable, in a single day, of displacing even the king of gods from his throne by his valour."

sanskrit: kiṃ punar dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraṃ durdyūtadevinam vidviṣṭaṃ sarvalokasya dambhalobhaparāyaṇam
english: "How much more then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who cheats at dice, who is hated by all the world, given over to arrogance and greed."

sanskrit: mātaraṃ caiva śocāmi kṛpaṇāṃ putragṛddhinīm yāsmākaṃ nityam āśāste mahattvam adhikaṃ paraiḥ
english: "And I grieve for my pitiable mother, who longs for her sons, who always hopes for our greatness beyond that of rivals."

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu tasyānāthāyā madvināśād bhujaṃgama aphalās te bhaviṣyanti mayi sarve manorathāḥ
english: "How, O serpent, at my death, will all those longings she placed in me become fruitless for that helpless one?"

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca yamajau guruvartinau madbāhubalasaṃstabdhau nityaṃ puruṣamāninau
english: "Nakula and Sahadeva, the twin brothers who are obedient to their elders — ever relying on the strength of my arms, they always pride themselves as men."

sanskrit: nirutsāhau bhaviṣyete bhraṣṭavīryaparākramau madvināśāt paridyūnāv iti me vartate matiḥ
english: "At my death they will become dispirited, their valour and prowess stripped away, afflicted and sorrowful — so my mind turns."

sanskrit: evaṃvidhaṃ bahu tadā vilalāpa vṛkodaraḥ bhujaṃgabhogasaṃruddho nāśakac ca viceṣṭitum
english: Thus Vṛkodara lamented greatly in various ways, bound by the serpent's coils and unable to stir.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu kaunteya babhūvāsvasthacetanaḥ aniṣṭadarśanān ghorān utpātān paricintayan
english: Meanwhile Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, became uneasy of mind, pondering the dreadful and ill-omened portents he was witnessing.

sanskrit: dāruṇaṃ hy aśivaṃ nādaṃ śivā dakṣiṇataḥ sthitā dīptāyāṃ diśi vitrastā rauti tasyāśramasya ha
english: For a jackal, standing to the south in the blazing quarter, terrified, was uttering a fierce and inauspicious howl near that hermitage.

sanskrit: ekapakṣākṣicaraṇā vartikā ghoradarśanā rudhiraṃ vamantī dadṛśe pratyādityam apasvarā
english: A quail, hideous to behold, with one wing, one eye, and one foot, was seen vomiting blood toward the sun, crying with ill omens.

sanskrit: pravavāv anilo rūkṣaś caṇḍaḥ śarkarakarṣaṇaḥ apasavyāni sarvāṇi mṛgapakṣirutāni ca
english: A harsh and violent wind blew, dragging gravel along, and all the cries of beasts and birds went in the inauspicious direction.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato vāyasaḥ kṛṣṇo yāhi yāhīti vāśati muhur muhuḥ prasphurati dakṣiṇo 'sya bhujas tathā
english: A black crow behind him cawed again and again "Go, go!" and his right arm throbbed repeatedly.

sanskrit: hṛdayaṃ caraṇaś cāpi vāmo 'sya parivartate savyasyākṣṇo vikāraś cāpy aniṣṭaḥ samapadyata
english: His heart and left foot twitched, and an inauspicious change came over his left eye.

sanskrit: sa dharmarājo medhāvī śaṅkamāno mahad bhayam draupadīṃ paripapraccha kva bhīma iti bhārata
english: That wise Dharma-king, suspecting some great calamity, asked Draupadī: "Where is Bhīma?" — O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śaśaṃsa tasmai pāñcālī cirayātaṃ vṛkodaram sa pratasthe mahābāhur dhaumyena sahito nṛpaḥ
english: The Pāñcālī princess told him of Vṛkodara who had gone for a long while; and the mighty-armed king set out accompanied by Dhaumya.

sanskrit: draupadyā rakṣaṇaṃ kāryam ity uvāca dhanaṃjayam nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca vyādideśa dvijān prati
english: "Draupadī must be guarded" — so he commanded Dhanañjaya, and he instructed Nakula and Sahadeva regarding the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: sa tasya padam unnīya tasmād evāśramāt prabhuḥ dadarśa pṛthivīṃ cihnair bhīmasya paricihnitām
english: That lord, tracking his footprints, departing from that very hermitage, saw the earth marked with the signs left by Bhīma.

sanskrit: dhāvatas tasya vīrasya mṛgārthe vātaraṃhasaḥ ūruvātavinirbhagnān drumān vyāvarjitān pathi
english: Of that hero running with the speed of the wind in pursuit of game, trees broken by the blast of his thighs were flung aside along the path.

sanskrit: sa gatvā tais tadā cihnair dadarśa girigahvare gṛhītaṃ bhujagendreṇa niśceṣṭam anujaṃ tathā
english: Following those very signs, he went and beheld in a mountain cave his younger brother, seized by the king of serpents, lying motionless.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yudhiṣṭhiras tam āsādya sarpabhogābhiveṣṭitam dayitaṃ bhrātaraṃ vīram idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Yudhiṣṭhira, approaching that beloved heroic brother who was encircled by the serpent's coils, spoke these words:

sanskrit: kuntīmātaḥ katham imām āpadaṃ tvam avāptavān kaś cāyaṃ parvatābhogapratimaḥ pannagottamaḥ
english: "O son of Kuntī, how have you fallen into this calamity? And who is this best of serpents, resembling the very coil of a mountain?"

sanskrit: sa dharmarājam ālakṣya bhrātā bhrātaram agrajam kathayām āsa tat sarvaṃ grahaṇādi viceṣṭitam
english: That brother, perceiving the Dharma-king, his elder brother, related to him all that had happened from his seizure onward.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca devo vā yadi vā daitya urago vā bhavān yadi satyaṃ sarpa vaco brūhi pṛcchati tvāṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Whether you are a god, a Daitya, or a serpent — if you are willing to speak truly, O snake, Yudhiṣṭhira asks you."

sanskrit: kim āhṛtya viditvā vā prītis te syād bhujaṃgama kim āhāraṃ prayacchāmi kathaṃ muñced bhavān imam
english: "What, if brought or known, would please you, O serpent? What food shall I offer you? How will you release this one?"

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca nahuṣo nāma rājāham āsaṃ pūrvas tavānagha prathitaḥ pañcamaḥ somād āyoḥ putro narādhipa
english: The serpent said: "I was the king named Nahuṣa, your ancestor, O sinless one — the celebrated fifth son descended from Soma through Āyu, O lord of men."

sanskrit: kratubhis tapasā caiva svādhyāyena damena ca trailokyaiśvaryam avyagraṃ prāpto vikramaṇena ca
english: "Through sacrifices, through austerity, through self-study, through self-restraint, and through conquest, I obtained uncontested sovereignty over the three worlds."

sanskrit: tad aiśvaryaṃ samāsādya darpo mām agamat tadā sahasraṃ hi dvijātīnām uvāha śibikāṃ mama
english: "Having obtained that sovereignty, pride overtook me at that time — for a thousand twice-born ones carried my palanquin."

sanskrit: aiśvaryamadamatto 'ham avamanya tato dvijān imām agastyena daśām ānītaḥ pṛthivīpate
english: "I, intoxicated with the pride of sovereignty, disrespected the Brāhmaṇas — and by Agastya I was brought to this condition, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: na tu mām ajahāt prajñā yāvad adyeti pāṇḍava tasyaivānugrahād rājann agastyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "Yet my wisdom has not left me even until today — by the grace of that great-souled Agastya himself, O king, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭhe kāle mamāhāraḥ prāpto 'yam anujas tava nāham enaṃ vimokṣyāmi na cānyam abhikāmaye
english: "This younger brother of yours has come as my food at the sixth meal-time; I shall not release him, and I desire no other."

sanskrit: praśnān uccāritāṃs tu tvaṃ vyāhariṣyasi cen mama atha paścād vimokṣyāmi bhrātaraṃ te vṛkodaram
english: "But if you shall answer the questions I have propounded, then afterwards I shall release your brother Vṛkodara."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brūhi sarpa yathākāmaṃ prativakṣyāmi te vacaḥ api cec chaknuyāṃ prītim āhartuṃ te bhujaṃgama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Ask, O serpent, as you please — I shall answer your words, if I am able to bring satisfaction to you, O serpent."

sanskrit: vedyaṃ yad brāhmaṇeneha tad bhavān vetti kevalam sarparāja tataḥ śrutvā prativakṣyāmi te vacaḥ
english: "What a Brāhmaṇa must know here — that you alone know, O king of serpents; having heard it from you, I shall then answer your words."

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca brāhmaṇaḥ ko bhaved rājan vedyaṃ kiṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira bravīhy atimatiṃ tvāṃ hi vākyair anumimīmahe
english: The serpent said: "Who is a Brāhmaṇa, O king? And what is to be known, O Yudhiṣṭhira? Speak — for we shall judge your great intellect by your words."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca satyaṃ dānaṃ kṣamā śīlam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ damo ghṛṇā dṛśyante yatra nāgendra sa brāhmaṇa iti smṛtaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Where truth, charity, forbearance, good conduct, non-cruelty, self-restraint, and compassion are seen, O king of serpents — he is remembered as a Brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: vedyaṃ sarpa paraṃ brahma nirduḥkham asukhaṃ ca yat yatra gatvā na śocanti bhavataḥ kiṃ vivakṣitam
english: "What is to be known, O serpent, is the supreme Brahman — that which is beyond sorrow and beyond joy, going whereto one grieves no more. What is your intent in asking?"

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca cāturvarṇyaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca satyaṃ ca brahma caiva ha śūdreṣv api ca satyaṃ ca dānam akrodha eva ca ānṛśaṃsyam ahiṃsā ca ghṛṇā caiva yudhiṣṭhira
english: The serpent said: "The four-caste order is the authority, and truth and Brahman as well — and even among Śūdras there is truth, charity, freedom from anger, non-cruelty, non-violence, and compassion also, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: vedyaṃ yac cāttha nirduḥkham asukhaṃ ca narādhipa tābhyāṃ hīnaṃ padaṃ cānyan na tad astīti lakṣaye
english: "As for what you said is to be known — that beyond sorrow and beyond joy, O lord of men — I hold that there is no other state inferior to those two, none whatsoever."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śūdre caitad bhavel lakṣyaṃ dvije tac ca na vidyate na vai śūdro bhavec chūdro brāhmaṇo na ca brāhmaṇaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "If this mark were found in a Śūdra, and not found in a twice-born — then the Śūdra would not be a Śūdra, and the Brāhmaṇa would not be a Brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: yatraital lakṣyate sarpa vṛttaṃ sa brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ yatraitan na bhavet sarpa taṃ śūdram iti nirdiśet
english: "Where this conduct is seen, O serpent, he is remembered as a Brāhmaṇa; where this is not present, O serpent, that one should be designated as a Śūdra."

sanskrit: yat punar bhavatā proktaṃ na vedyaṃ vidyateti ha tābhyāṃ hīnam atītyātra padaṃ nāstīti ced api
english: "As for what you further said — that there is nothing to be known beyond those two — if indeed there is no state beyond them, going past both,"

sanskrit: evam etan mataṃ sarpa tābhyāṃ hīnaṃ na vidyate yathā śītoṣṇayor madhye bhaven noṣṇaṃ na śītatā
english: "So too is this my view, O serpent — nothing exists inferior to those two; just as between cold and hot there can be neither heat nor coldness."
